items.title: Quantum Computing 101: Can a Cat be Alive and Dead at The Same Time?
items.summary:
The Insider Brief:

Qubits, unlike classical bits, can exist in a superposition of 0 and 1, the idea Schrödinger’s famous cat was invented to illustrate. Entanglement links qubits in ways classical computers struggle to simulate at scale.

Superconducting qubits must be cooled to around 10 thousandths of a degree above absolute zero, far colder than outer space, to protect their fragile quantum states.

Quantum computers won’t replace laptops, but they could transform the simulation of molecules and materials and break today’s public-key encryption, which is driving the shift to post-quantum cryptography.

Everyone in quantum gets the same questions from friends, family and colleagues outside the field. What is a qubit, really? Why do quantum computers need to be so cold? And will one replace my laptop? Here are the short answers.

A classical computer stores information in bits, each either 0 or 1. A quantum computer uses qubits. Like a bit, a qubit gives a 0 or a 1 when you measure it. Before it is measured, though, it can be in a superposition: a combination of 0 and 1 at the same time, with each outcome carrying a certain probability.

Schrödinger’s cat

items.title: Gyeonggi Province Holds Forum on Quantum and Semiconductor Industry Cooperation
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Gyeonggi Province hosted a quantum industry forum and networking event bringing together companies, researchers and government representatives to discuss industry development and commercialisation.

Five companies presented R&D achievements in areas including quantum sensing, semiconductor inspection, quantum computer components and processing equipment.

Gyeonggi Province is providing KRW 3 billion this year to support quantum-related companies and talent development, while linking quantum technology with its semiconductor and advanced industries.

PRESS RELEASE — The ‘Gyeonggi Quantum Innovation Forum and 2026 Gyeonggi Quantum-Semiconductor Convergence Industry Networking Day’, hosted by Gyeonggi Province and the Gyeonggi Business and Science Accelerator and organised by Sungkyunkwan University’s Anchor Project Group and the Korea Nanotechnology Institute, was held on the 25th at the Novotel Ambassador Suwon.

The event brought together stakeholders from Gyeonggi Province’s quantum ecosystem to discuss cooperation and commercialisation opportunities. Attendees included Kim Tae-hyung, Chairman of the Future Science and Cooperation Committee of the Gyeonggi Provincial Council; Park Min-kyung, Director of the Semiconductor Industry Division of Gyeonggi Province; representatives from Sungkyunkwan University and the Korea Nanotechnology Institute; industry, academic and research experts; companies receiving R&D support for quantum industry projects in Gyeonggi Province; and representatives from related organisations.

In his congratulatory remarks, Kim Tae-hyung, Chairman of the Future Science and Cooperation Committee of the Gyeonggi Provincial Council, said, “Gyeonggi Province has already established a foundation for developing the quantum industry through the enactment of relevant ordinances. Quantum technology has now reached a stage where it can be applied directly to everyday life, much like the PangtaG Bus, the autonomous bus operating in Pangyo. As the quantum industry is a key driver of future growth, the Provincial Council will support the expansion of policy and institutional measures and cooperation frameworks.”

items.title: Equal1 Selected to Advance in EIC STEP Scale Up Program For Potential Equity Investment of up to €30 Million
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Irish quantum computing company Equal1 advanced to due diligence for a potential equity investment of up to €30 million from the European Innovation Council Fund.

Equal1 would use the funding to expand production and deployment of its on-premises quantum computers.

The University College Dublin spinout uses standard CMOS manufacturing processes to integrate silicon spin qubits, control electronics and error correction on a single chip.

PRESS RELEASE — Equal1 today announced it has been selected to advance to the due-diligence phase with the European Innovation Council (EIC) Fund under the Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform (STEP) Scale Up program. The selection opens the path for a potential equity investment of up to €30 million.

The prospective EIC investment will accelerate Equal1 ’s commercialization roadmap, scale the production and deployment of its on-premise quantum computing solutions, and strengthen Europe’s technological sovereignty in quantum computing.

Equal1 , a University College Dublin (UCD) spinout, is pioneering the integration of quantum silicon spin qubits, control electronics and error correction integrated in CMOS silicon and fabricated using standard CMOS semiconductor technology. This approach eliminates the massive infrastructure barriers associated with legacy quantum systems, advancing the company’s vision to make quantum computing as commonplace and transformative as GPUs.

items.title: Ethereum Plans Shift to Hash-Based Signatures for Post-Quantum Security
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Ethereum developers are planning to replace the network’s elliptic-curve signatures with hash-based alternatives as part of a security effort targeting future quantum and potential AI-driven cryptographic threats.

The proposed changes cover validator signatures, wallet accounts and data blob commitments, with Keccak-256 emerging as the preferred hash function.

The Ethereum Foundation is targeting December 2029 for the migration, although larger signatures, wallet upgrades and increased node costs remain technical challenges.

Photo from Pexels by Jonathan Borba .

Ethereum’s core developers are preparing to phase out the elliptic-curve cryptography that secures the network and switch to hash-based signatures, a change meant to protect against attacks powered by quantum computers or by advances in artificial intelligence, Crypto Briefing reported . The plan was set out in a series of blog posts under the PQAI banner, published on November 23 and 24, 2026.

The first entry, PQAI #0, made the move to hash-based signatures a top agenda item for the Foundation, according to the outlet. Crypto Briefing also reported that the Foundation has doubled the size of its protocol security team. The Foundation’s dedicated post-quantum team was formed in January 2026, as The Quantum Insider reported when the Foundation made post-quantum security a top strategic priority.

items.title: Bank of England Urges Firms to Move Faster on Quantum Security
items.summary:
Insider Brief

The Bank of England urged systemically important financial firms to adopt quantum-resistant cryptography ahead of the U.K.’s national timetable, warning that delays at shared suppliers could disrupt services across the sector.

A sufficiently powerful quantum computer could enable forged digital signatures and expose sensitive financial records that attackers collect today for future decryption.

The U.K. roadmap calls for migration plans by the end of 2028, priority upgrades by the end of 2031 and full migration by the end of 2035.

The Bank of England urged financial firms with the greatest impact on the stability of the U.K. financial system to move faster than the national timetable for adopting quantum-resistant cryptography, warning that delays at a single technology provider could disrupt services at several firms at once.

In its November Financial Stability Report , the central bank’s Financial Policy Committee made an orderly shift to post-quantum cryptography an immediate priority. The committee had already urged firms to start planning. It says institutions whose disruption would have the biggest consequences for the wider financial system should get ahead of the milestones set out by the U.K.’s National Cyber Security Centre.

The U.K. roadmap calls on organizations to identify where they use cryptography. Then, they are asked to draw up a migration plan by the end of 2028, complete their highest-priority upgrades by the end of 2031 and finish the transition by the end of 2035. The committee called for systemically important firms to move sooner without specifying new dates for them.

items.title: SAP and planqc Expand Quantum Computing Partnership, Plan Hardware Tests in 2027
items.summary:
Insider Brief

SAP and planqc expanded their collaboration and demonstrated a cloud interface linking SAP enterprise software to planqc’s neutral-atom quantum computing platform.

In a live logistics demo, SAP sent a beverage truck-loading problem to a quantum simulator and received a loading plan back in its software.

The companies plan to begin testing business applications on planqc’s neutral-atom quantum hardware in 2027.

PRESS RELEASE — SAP and planqc are expanding their collaboration in quantum computing. At the Quantum Day Munich by SAP, the two companies demonstrated the first live integration of a planqc neutral-atom quantum computer into an SAP environment. This marks an important step towards making quantum computing capabilities directly accessible to business applications.

The integration is enabled by a cloud interface connecting SAP applications with planqc’s quantum hardware. At the Quantum Day Munich by SAP, held at the SAP Campus in Garching, the companies also demonstrated how quantum computing can be incorporated into existing business processes through an initial logistics use case: optimizing the loading of delivery trucks.

Neutral-Atom Quantum Computing for Industrial Applications
